problem: Given that ${i,j,k}$ is the standard basis of ${R}^{3}$ and that the images of $i,$ $j,$ and $k$ under the action of a linear transformation $T$ are $⟨3,2,-1⟩,$ $⟨2,-3,1⟩,$ and $⟨1,-2,3⟩,$ respectively, what is the standard matrix of $T?$
worked_solution:
Every linear transformation in ${R}^{3}$ can be represented as a $3\times 3$ matrix. The standard matrix representation of the transformation has columns that are the images of the vectors $i,j,$ and $k$ under the action of the transformation.

Therefore, the standard matrix for the linear transformation is 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & 2 & 1 \\ 2 & -3 & -2 \\ -1 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}].
$$
